description: Retaliation charges totalled 42,301 in FY2024 - the most prevalent filing for the seventeenth consecutive year. In FY2021 it appeared in 56.0% of all charges filed.
energy_note: More than four in ten charges, every year, for seventeen years.

description: It attaches to every other charge type: a person files a discrimination complaint and is then dismissed, and the dismissal is a separate claim. One dispute generates two harms.
energy_note: Complaining creates a second, fresh injury.

aspect: The subtle forms are the common ones
description: Exclusion from meetings, isolation from colleagues, denial of leave, relocation to a smaller office, unrealistic targets. The legal test is whether it would dissuade a reasonable employee from raising a concern - and small things do.
energy_note: Nothing dramatic. Just everything, slightly worse.

description: Eleven weeks after the grievance, a reorganisation is announced. Her role is not deleted. It is moved under someone two levels below her previous reporting line, and her project is given to the person she complained about. 'This isn't about you. It's been in planning since the spring.'
energy_note: A restructure that has been in planning since the spring.

aspect: Women report more retaliation than men
description: Research finds female whistleblowers experience more retaliation than men, which compounds every gendered category in this file.
energy_note: Reporting it is worse for her than for him.
